faqs.a: The quoted rate is the nominal annual rate. Because interest is added to your balance each quarter and then earns interest itself, the effective annual yield is higher — 7.19% in our example versus the quoted 7%. The calculator shows both.
faqs.q: What is the difference between the FD rate and the effective yield?

faqs.a: Slightly. More frequent compounding means interest starts earning interest sooner. On a 5-year deposit the difference between monthly and quarterly compounding is small — usually a fraction of a percent — but it is real money on large deposits.
faqs.q: Is monthly compounding better than quarterly?

faqs.a: Banks typically pay the rate for the period the money actually stayed, minus a penalty of about 1%. You also lose the compounding benefit of the full tenure. Use the calculator to compare the maturity value against what you would get by breaking it.
faqs.q: What happens if I break my FD early?

faqs.a: Yes. In India FD interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate, and banks deduct TDS above a threshold. The maturity value shown here is before tax.

For the same rate and tenure, a lump-sum FD grows more because the full amount compounds from day one. A recurring deposit builds up gradually, so less money earns interest for less time. Choose an FD if you have the lump sum ready.
faqs.q: FD or recurring deposit — which grows more?

faqs.a: Your principal is safe up to the deposit insurance limit (₹5 lakh per depositor per bank in India). The real risk is inflation: if prices rise faster than your FD rate, your purchasing power shrinks even as the balance grows.

fixed-deposit-calculator.formula:
Maturity A = P x (1 + r/n)^(n x t), where P = principal, r = annual rate (decimal), n = compounding periods per year, t = years.
Interest earned = A - P.
Effective annual yield = (1 + r/n)^n - 1.
howTo: Enter the amount you want to deposit.
Enter the annual interest rate offered by your bank.
Choose the tenure in years and the compounding frequency.
Read the maturity value, total interest, and effective annual yield instantly.
keyFacts: A fixed deposit locks your money for a fixed tenure at a fixed interest rate.
Interest is usually compounded quarterly in India, which lifts the effective yield above the quoted rate.
Longer tenures and higher rates both increase the maturity value, but the rate matters more.
Breaking an FD early usually costs a penalty of around 1% on the rate, plus the lost compounding.
FD interest is taxable as income in most countries, including India.
